claim: Tongeren is the oldest town in Belgium, founded as Roman Atuatuca Tungrorum and serving as the only Roman administrative capital within Belgium's modern borders.
quote: Tongeren holds the distinction of being the oldest town in Belgium, as the only Roman administrative capital within the country's borders. As a Roman settlement, it was known as Atuatuca Tungrorum and served as the capital of the Civitas Tungrorum district.

claim: Atuatuca Tungrorum is documented in the Princeton Encyclopedia of Classical Sites as the Roman name for Tongeren/Tongres.
The Gallo-Romeins Museum is open Tue-Fri 9-17, weekends and Belgian public holidays 10-18, closed Mondays; during Flemish school holidays Tue-Fri is 10-18.
quote: Tuesday–Friday: 9 a.m. – 5 p.m. Saturday–Sunday and Belgian public holidays: 10 a.m. – 6 p.m. Closed Mondays (except when a Monday falls on a public holiday). Tuesday – Friday during school holidays (Flanders): 10 a.m. – 6 p.m.

claim: Gallo-Romeins Museum admission is €8 adult, €5 senior 65+/student/disabled, €1 children 4-18.
quote: Adults: €8.00 Seniors (65+): €5.00 Students: €5.00 Children (4-18): €1.00 People with Disability: €5.00 Teachers: €5.00

claim: The Gallo-Romeins Museum won the European Museum of the Year Award in 2011 — the first Belgian museum to receive that prize; later also winner of the 2014 Museum Prize and the 2016 Romulus Prize.
quote: The museum gained international recognition when it was awarded the European Museum of the Year Award in 2011, becoming the first Belgian museum to receive this honor.

claim: The Tongeren Sunday antique market runs every Sunday year-round from 07:00 to 13:00 with more than 350 exhibitors plus ~40 antique shops.
quote: Every Sunday from 7 am to 1 pm. more than 350 exhibitors and some 40 antique shops

claim: The market is officially branded as the largest antique and brocante market in the Benelux.
quote: Antiekmarkt TONGEREN De grootste antiek- en brocantemarkt in de Benelux

claim: The market sprawls across the Leopoldwal and surrounding streets; Tongeren on Sunday morning attracts international crowds (Dutch, German, French, British, American).
quote: Tongeren is an international city on Sunday mornings, attracting an increasing number of Dutch, Germans, French, British and Americans.

claim: Parking strategy: free parking at Tongeren train station is a short walk to the market; the Julianus garage (first floor) sits inside the market footprint, and ring-road parking fills up early.
quote: Parking is free at the train station, and it is a quick walk to the market... You can park on the 1st floor of Julianus car park in Tongeren, which is directly part of the market area.

claim: The bronze Ambiorix statue on the Grote Markt (1866, sculptor Jules Bertin) commemorates the Eburones king's 54 BCE victory over Caesar's legions and is the city's iconic landmark.
quote: The imposing bronze statue of Ambiorix, King of the Eburones, dating from 1866 is a tribute to his memorable victory over the Romans in 54 BCE.

claim: The Tongeren beguinage was founded in 1257 and is one of 13 Flemish béguinages inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1998.
quote: Thirteen Flemish Béguinages gained the status as a UNESCO World Heritage in 1998. The Flemish Béguinage of Tongeren is part of this UNESCO World Heritage... The béguinage was founded in 1257.

claim: The Gothic Onze-Lieve-Vrouwebasiliek replaced an earlier Romanesque church burnt down in 1240 and took more than 300 years to complete; its bell tower is UNESCO-listed (as part of the Belfries of Belgium and France, 1999).
quote: The construction of the present Gothic church began in 1240 after the old Romanesque church here burnt down. It took more than 300 years to build it and today its imposing bell tower is included on the UNESCO World Heritage List.

claim: Roman defensive wall stretches still survive in the fields beyond the medieval town; the 1241 medieval wall reused Roman masonry after an attack by Duke Hendrik of Brabant.
quote: The Medieval town wall was built in 1241 after an attack by Duke Hendrik of Brabant. Some of those Roman stones came quite handy for its construction.

claim: Driving distance Lanaken to Tongeren is roughly 22 km via Riemst, around 19 minutes by car.
quote: the distance from Lanaken to Tongeren is 22 kilometers via the road, with a route duration of approximately 19 minutes and going via Riemst
